notes: Private event-driven fund deck for institutional one-on-one meetings in which a no-losing-year claim is contradicted by the deck's own 2022 return and a trough-dated window is used as a highlight, alongside a private-fund track record legitimately shown without 1-, 5- and 10-year periods and a fully disclosed hypothetical allocation.

planted.span: Capital preservation comes first: the Fund has never finished a calendar year in negative territory, through the 2018 selloff, the 2020 drawdown and the 2022 rate shock.
planted.explanation: The statement is untrue on the deck's own Slide 4 table, which shows 2022 at -1.2% gross and -3.0% net of fees.

planted.span: The last restructuring cycle shows what the strategy can do: from the March 23, 2020 market low through June 30, 2021, the Fund returned 71.4% net of fees.
planted.explanation: The window starts at the market trough and ends on a chosen mid-2021 date, producing a figure far above the full calendar-year results for the same stretch (21.6% net in 2020 and 15.8% net in 2021), so the period is selected in a way that is not fair and balanced.

decoys.span: Annualized since inception, January 1, 2017 through December 31, 2025: 11.5% gross of fees and 7.8% net of fees.
decoys.why_ok: The Fund is a private fund, so the 1-, 5- and 10-year requirement does not apply, and every calendar year since inception is shown with gross and net at equal prominence.

decoys.span: A hypothetical portfolio of 54% global equities, 36% U.S. investment-grade bonds and 10% in the Fund, rebalanced each January 1, would have returned 7.98% annualized from 2017 through 2025, versus 7.96% for a 60/40 portfolio without the Fund; its worst calendar year (2022) would have been -14.9% rather than -16.2%.
decoys.why_ok: The illustration is labeled hypothetical, limited to institutional one-on-one meetings under written policies, and followed by the indices, weights, rebalancing and fee assumptions used (no adviser fee on the index sleeves, and the Fund sleeve taken net of all Fund fees and expenses) and by its risks and limitations, and its figures reconcile to the Slide 4 net returns.
